$comment: Design tokens. Layers reference these BY NAME and may never hard-code a value — that is what makes themes and per-user colour profiles possible without regenerating the style.

$enums.$comment: Vocabularies a categorical colour mode can be declared over. A mode bound to an enum MUST colour every member — that is how `unknown` and `default_only` cannot be silently forgotten (doc 10 ⑨ / ㉜).

$naming: Token names leak into UI copy, so they must not assert anything false. These two were `water.regulated` / `water.other`, which implied some BC water is UNREGULATED. None is: every stream and lake is covered by the general rules for its region and Management Unit. The real distinction is whether WE hold a water-specific record — 2.4% do, 97.6% do not — so the names now describe OUR COVERAGE, not legal status. A toast reading 'no rules held for this water' teaches the single most dangerous inference this app can teach; 'no rules specific to this water — the general rules below apply' does not.
